title: Conditions for health

blocks.heading: Conditions for health
blocks.text: Clean water, hygiene, an adequate diet, prevention and treatment of disease, and social conditions can influence health and life expectancy. Life expectancy is an average under the mortality conditions used, not an individual promise. Poverty can restrict food, housing and service access; stress and illness can interact with those constraints.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Water and hygiene
blocks.text: Safe water and appropriate hygiene reduce exposure to some contamination pathways. A supply needs reliable access and protection after collection; a new water point does not help equally if distance, breakdown or unsafe handling prevents use.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Adequate diet
blocks.text: A nutritionally adequate diet provides suitable energy and nutrients for health. Availability, affordability and varied intake matter. More food by weight does not necessarily establish adequate nutrition, and a household label does not diagnose nutritional status.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Disease prevention and care
blocks.text: Prevention and effective accessible care can reduce illness and its consequences. Facilities, trained staff, supplies and timely referral must work together. A building without operating support does not establish useful health provision.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Poverty and stress
blocks.text: Material hardship can limit adequate food, housing and service access, while insecurity and stress can affect well-being. Illness can also reduce earnings and add care costs. Explain interacting pathways without assuming poverty establishes an individual’s health or assigning blame.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Follow the mechanism
blocks.text: Explain the access mechanism in an invented village with a safe water point that repeatedly breaks and households then collecting from an unprotected source. Breakdowns remove reliable safe access and push collection towards a less protected source. Maintenance addresses the reliability link, rather than counting the installed point as continuous coverage.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to Population (7.1), Development (1.1) and Education (7.3). Separate installed facilities, usable coverage and health outcomes. Synthetic figures model reasoning and are not current Namibian statistics.
